definitions.explanation: The act of meeting someone in person, especially for the first time or after a long separation. Also used as a modifier to mean 'in-person' as opposed to online.

examples.japanese: {初|はじ}めての{対面|たいめん}だった。
examples.english: It was our first face-to-face meeting.

examples.japanese: {対面|たいめん}での{授業|じゅぎょう}が{再開|さいかい}された。
{何年|なんねん}もオンラインだけでやりとりしていたが、やっと{対面|たいめん}で{会|あ}うことができた。
examples.english: After years of only communicating online, we finally met in person.

notes:
USAGE AS SURU-VERB: {対面|たいめん}する means "to meet face-to-face." Example: {長年|ながねん}{会|あ}えなかった{父|ちち}と{対面|たいめん}した。(I met with my father, whom I hadn't seen for years.)

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {対面|たいめん}する: to meet face-to-face
- {対面|たいめん}での〜: in-person ~ (classes, meetings, etc.)
- {初|はつ}{対面|たいめん}: first meeting
- {感動|かんどう}の{対面|たいめん}: an emotional reunion

MODERN USAGE: Since the COVID-19 pandemic, {対面|たいめん} has become widely used as a modifier meaning "in-person" as opposed to オンライン (online), as in {対面|たいめん}{授業|じゅぎょう} (in-person classes) vs. オンライン{授業|じゅぎょう} (online classes).
